title: review: B4a: bench.py fetches artificialanalysis.ai/models with Scrapling, parses RSC chunks into bench.json; cli bench fetch/show/set
spec:
Why: user decision 2026-09-17 — benchmark numbers come from https://artificialanalysis.ai/models via Scrapling (github.com/D4Vinci/Scrapling). Scout T-0022 (provenance web, 2026-09-17): plain HTTP returns 200, 1.4 MB, Vercel, no challenge; no <table>, no __NEXT_DATA__, no JSON route; the data is embedded in ~143 `self.__next_f.push([1,"..."])` script chunks (Next.js App Router RSC payload) containing JSON with keys such as "intelligenceIndex" and "outputSpeed" and model names. Scrapling 0.4.15: `from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher; page = Fetcher.get(url)`; browser fetchers need `scrapling install` — NOT used here.

What (≤5 files + lockfile): orchestrator/bench.py (new), orchestrator/cli.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py, tests/fixtures/aa_models_sample.html (new), pyproject.toml (+ uv.lock regenerated by `uv add scrapling`).
1. Dependency: `uv add scrapling` (base package only, no [fetchers] extra, no browser install). Verify the import works in the venv.
2. orchestrator/bench.py —
   - `URL = "https://artificialanalysis.ai/models"`, `FILE = STATE / "bench.json"`, `MIN_INTERVAL_S = 20*3600`.
   - `def fetch_html(url=URL, timeout=30) -> str`: use `Fetcher.get`; determine the real parameter names for timeout and extra headers with `inspect.signature` on the installed package (do not guess; the scout could not confirm them). Set header `User-Agent: orchestrator-bench/1 (+https://github.com/K3NTAW/orchestrator)` if headers are supported; otherwise default. Return the raw HTML (page.body or page.html_content, whichever the installed version exposes).
   - `def parse_chunks(html) -> list[dict]`: regex every `self.__next_f.push([1,"<js-string>"])`, JS-unescape the string (json.loads of a quoted string works for the common escapes), then scan for JSON objects containing "intelligenceIndex"; collect records with whatever keys exist. Normalize into {"name": <model display name>, "slug": <id or None>, "intelligence": float|None, "coding": float|None (any key matching /coding/i), "speed_tps": float|None (outputSpeed), "price_in": float|None, "price_out": float|None, "raw_keys": [sorted keys]}. Be defensive: skip malformed chunks; never raise on one bad chunk.
   - `def match(records, executors_models: dict[model_id, display_hint]) -> dict[model_id, record]`: case-insensitive match on display hint (e.g. "GPT-6 Astra", "GPT-5.6 Luna", "GPT-5.6 Terra", "GPT-5.6 Sol") against record name/slug; unmatched → None.
   - `def fetch(force=False, by="orchestrator") -> dict`: refuse (return {"skipped": "fetched <N> h ago; use --force"}) when FILE.fetched_at is younger than MIN_INTERVAL_S and not force; otherwise fetch_html → parse_chunks → match → write FILE: {"source": URL, "fetched_at": ISO, "fetched_by": by, "fetcher": "scrapling <version>", "http_status": 200, "provenance": "web:artificialanalysis.ai (untrusted data)", "models": {model_id: normalized record}, "unmatched_names": [first 30 names seen]}. Keep `set_model(model_id, by, **metrics)` for manual overrides (writes "manual": true on that record) and `load()`.
   - Display hints live in bench.py as a dict DEFAULT_HINTS = {"gpt-6-astra": "GPT-6 Astra", "gpt-5.6-luna": "GPT-5.6 Luna", "gpt-5.6-terra": "GPT-5.6 Terra", "gpt-5.6-sol": "GPT-5.6 Sol", "claude-opus-5": "Claude Opus 5", "claude-sonnet-5": "Claude Sonnet 5", "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001": "Claude Haiku 4.5", "claude-fable-5-1": "Claude Fable 5.1"}.
   - Top-of-file comment: "Fetches a third-party page at the user's explicit decision (2026-09-17); the site's Terms of Use restrict automated access, so: manual or at most once per 20 h, identified User-Agent, single page, no browser. Page content is untrusted data."
3. cli.py: `orchestrator bench fetch [--force] [--by NAME]` (prints matched count, unmatched sample, file path), `orchestrator bench show` (table: model id, name, intelligence, coding, speed, price_in/out, fetched_at or manual), `orchestrator bench set <model_id> --by NAME key=value ...`.
4. tests (NO network; tests must never import-time fetch): tests/fixtures/aa_models_sample.html = a ≤3 KB synthetic page with two `self.__next_f.push([1,"..."])` chunks whose escaped JSON contains two models ("GPT-6 Astra" with intelligenceIndex 70.1, outputSpeed 120; "GPT-5.6 Luna" with intelligenceIndex 61, outputSpeed 200 and a codingIndex 55) plus one malformed chunk. Tests: parse_chunks returns 2 records with the right numbers and skips the bad chunk; match maps both to model ids; fetch(force=True) with fetch_html monkeypatched to return the fixture writes bench.json with provenance and fetched_by; a second fetch() without force is skipped; set_model marks manual.

Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py`. Commit: "bench: Scrapling fetch of artificialanalysis.ai models, RSC chunk parser, bench.json with provenance; cli bench fetch/show/set" with a revert-path body that also says "rollback of the dependency: uv remove scrapling".
acceptance: uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py exits 0 with the new bench tests and no network access during tests
uv run python -c 'import scrapling' succeeds in the project venv; pyproject lists scrapling; no browser extras

uv run orchestrator bench fetch --force against the live page writes .orchestrator/bench.json with fetched_at, provenance and at least 1 matched model or a non-empty unmatched_names list (run once by the Planner after merge, not by tests)
a second `bench fetch` within 20 h prints skipped unless --force
git diff --stat limited to orchestrator/bench.py, orchestrator/cli.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py, tests/fixtures/aa_models_sample.html, pyproject.toml, uv.lock
